plan.title: Colon treated vs control RSEM DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are RSEM gene-level expected counts (non-integer, 12000 genes x 12 samples) for a 6 treated vs 6 control unpaired colon design, single batch, with per-sample effective-length files unavailable and sample_01 flagged at ~4x below median library size. Because the effective-length-aware tximport/RSEM path cannot be used (the genes.results files were not delivered), the plan rounds RSEM expected counts to integers and proceeds on the standard DESeq2 raw-count path, explicitly flagging this deviation from the length-aware import that the grounded procedure prefers. Sample structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) runs first and reports the shallow sample's depth and clustering rather than silently dropping it, per the knowledge-service warning on library-size outliers. DESeq2 (Wald test, apeglm shrinkage, BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05) then identifies genes differing between treated and control, with edgeR quasi-likelihood run in parallel as the robustness cross-check the knowledge service recommends at n=6/group. Enrichment follows on the full ranked gene list (Wald statistic) against MSigDB Hallmark (staged locally) with Reactome as the confirmatory second collection, both of which are present in the reference store. A final report integrates DE tables, fit diagnostics, the overlap of the two DE methods, and the enrichment results with all required reproducibility metadata.

DESeqDataSetFromMatrix with ~condition, condition releveled to control as reference
